events.content:
View transitions are in place, and the app builds and serves both routes cleanly. This Next canary (16.4.0-canary.8) ships React's View Transition API in its default vendored React — `ViewTransition` and `addTransitionType` are exported directly from `react`, no experimental config flag needed (it's been removed from the config schema entirely) — so I built on those rather than hand-rolling `document.startViewTransition`.

**Shared element morph** — In `app/ProductGrid.tsx` each thumbnail is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={`product-image-${slug}`}>`, and `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` wraps the hero in the same name. On navigation React pairs the unmounting thumbnail with the mounting hero and the browser morphs position/size between them (timing tuned via `::view-transition-group(*)` in CSS).

**Directional slides** — New `app/TransitionLink.tsx` (client component) intercepts plain left-clicks, calls `addTransitionType('navigation-forward' | 'navigation-back')` inside `startTransition`, then does `router.push`. Modified clicks (cmd/ctrl/shift/middle-click) fall through to the browser. The root layout wraps `children` in a `<ViewTransition>` whose `update` prop maps those types to CSS classes: forward slides the old page out left / new in from the right, back does the reverse, and untyped navigations (e.g. browser back button) fall back to a cross-fade. Grid cards use `direction="forward"`, the detail page's back link uses `direction="back"`.

**Suspense transitions** — On both pages the Suspense fallback is wrapped in `<ViewTransition exit="suspense-fade">` and the content in `<ViewTransition enter="suspense-fade">`, so the skeleton cross-fades into content when it resolves instead of popping.

**Reduced motion** — A `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none !important` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements (which makes transitions complete instantly) and also stops the skeleton pulse animation.

Two supporting pieces: `types/react-view-transitions.d.ts` adds module-augmentation typings for `ViewTransition`/`addTransitionType` since `@types/react` 19 doesn't include them yet, and `next build` auto-added a `.next/dev/types` entry to `tsconfig.json`.

Verified: `npm run build` compiles and typechecks; `npm start` serves both routes with HTTP 200, and the SSR/RSC output contains all four `product-image-*` transition names, the navigation transition types, and the suspense-fade classes. One note: full morph/slide behavior needs a real browser to observe, which isn't available in this sandbox — but the wiring follows the documented React ViewTransition patterns exactly.
